Description Description We, representatives of the CIS Dota 2 community, as well as, in essence, a significant portion of the global Dota 2 player base, would like to formally express our deep concern regarding the current state of the game and its direction in recent years. Dota 2 has long been more than just a game for us - it is a competitive environment, a community, and a cultural phenomenon. However, many long-standing issues continue to negatively impact the player experience, and we believe they are not receiving the attention they deserve. Behavior Score System The current behavior score system is widely perceived as ineffective and, in many cases, unnecessary. Instead of improving match quality, it often creates frustration and imbalance. The system discourages communication between players, lacks fairness, and at times does not accurately reflect actual in-game behavior. As a result, it reduces overall enjoyment of the game. Ranked System The ranking system raises serious concerns. The gap between skill levels and MMR brackets is extremely large, making progression disproportionately difficult and time-consuming. For many players, ranking up requires an unrealistic investment of time, which reduces long-term engagement and motivation. Cheating and Fair Play One of the most critical issues is the growing presence of cheaters in public matches. This problem severely undermines competitive integrity. Many players believe that anti-cheat measures are insufficient and that enforcement actions are nearly nonexistent. A stronger and more transparent stance on fair play is urgently needed. Quality of Updates Recent updates are perceived as lacking depth, coherence, and clear direction. Changes often feel unfinished or disconnected from the needs of the community. This creates the impression that development is no longer guided by a clear vision for the game. Gameplay and Balance There is growing concern regarding the current gameplay direction and overall balance of the game. The meta is heavily dominated by aura-based items, which reduces strategic diversity and limits viable playstyles. Matches have shifted away from dynamic teamfights toward prolonged farming, making gameplay feel slower and less engaging. Additionally, the current comeback mechanics often lead to excessively long games, even in situations where one team has a clear advantage. Overall, there is a strong ощущение that player feedback is not being adequately considered, and that balance decisions are disconnected from the community’s expectations. Lack of Meaningful Events Over the past year, there has been a noticeable absence of engaging and memorable in-game events. Historically, events have played a key role in maintaining player interest and community enthusiasm. Their decline has led to a significant drop in overall engagement. Technical Issues, Bugs, and Server Stability There is growing concern regarding the overall technical condition of the game. Players frequently encounter bugs that remain unresolved for extended periods of time. In addition, server instability has become a recurring issue - matches can suffer from severe lag, sometimes lasting 30 minutes or more, directly impacting game outcomes and ruining the competitive experience. Furthermore, numerous visual and interface-related bugs reduce usability, negatively affecting play. Taken together, these issues create the impression of insufficient attention to the technical quality of the game. We are writing this not out of negativity, but out of genuine concern for the future of Dota 2. We believe in the game’s potential and its legacy, and we hope to see it thrive once again. We strongly urge greater transparency, closer communication with the community, and decisive action on the issues outlined above. Description I am writing to report a serious problem with the matchmaking system. I have more than 6900 hours in the game, and it has become extremely common for me to be placed in matches with accounts that have only 300–500 hours of total playtime. In many of these cases, these players clearly perform at a level that is far beyond what a legitimate player with that amount of experience should have. This strongly suggests that a large number of these accounts are smurf accounts created by experienced players. These accounts are not new players – they are experienced players using fresh accounts to bypass the matchmaking system. Because of this, the matchmaking quality is becoming worse. Instead of fair and balanced games, we end up with matches where smurf accounts completely distort the balance of the game. This creates a frustrating environment for players who have invested thousands of hours into the game. A player with 6900 hours should not regularly be matched with accounts that have only 300–400 hours, especially when those accounts clearly play at a much higher level than their experience suggests. This situation makes it feel like the matchmaking system is not effectively detecting or preventing smurfing, which seriously damages the competitive integrity of the game. Please investigate this issue and consider improving the detection of smurf accounts and the matchmaking system so that players with thousands of hours are not constantly placed in games with suspicious low-hour accounts. I would like to share some observations about the current Behavior Score and communication restriction system in Dota 2. I have been playing Dota since the Dota Allstars era (around 2004) and was also active during the time of dota-league.com, one of the earlier community platforms that already implemented matchmaking, reporting systems, and moderation. Having played the game for more than 20 years with very few breaks, I have followed the evolution of its systems quite closely. This post is not meant as a complaint, but rather as long-term player feedback about some interactions in the current system that may produce unintended effects on player behavior and match quality. Dota 2 relies heavily on coordination and information exchange between players. During matches, players often need to communicate things such as ultimate cooldowns, teleport cooldowns, buyback availability, or the need to delay a fight until certain abilities are available. These kinds of details can strongly influence the outcome of fights and objectives. When players receive communication restrictions due to Behavior Score penalties, it becomes difficult to communicate this type of information. As a result, teammates may misinterpret certain decisions during a match. For example, a player might not join a fight because abilities are on cooldown, because the engagement is clearly lost, or because positioning or farming for the next objective is the safer decision. Without communication, these decisions can easily appear as intentional non-cooperation. Reports are typically submitted during or immediately after matches. At that point, it may not yet be clear whether a decision that appeared questionable during the game was actually strategically correct. For instance, refusing to follow a teammate into a lost engagement may look negative in the moment but can later turn out to be the correct macro decision for the team. Because reports happen immediately, they can sometimes reflect frustration in the moment rather than an objective evaluation of behavior. When communication is limited, players also cannot explain their reasoning during the match. This may increase misunderstandings and lead to additional reports. I understand that Valve likely uses background systems to evaluate report accuracy over time, but restricted communication may still contribute to a feedback loop where misunderstandings increase reports and reports further reduce communication. From earlier community-run systems such as dota-league.com, reporting mechanisms also existed. Those systems were simpler and largely player-driven, but they often focused on clearly disruptive behavior. They also included moderation steps such as report reviews, cooldowns, temporary bans, and bans for multi-accounting to prevent players from bypassing penalties. While the system itself was simpler, enforcement against multi-accounting made it harder to circumvent the intended penalties. In the current environment, creating new accounts is relatively easy. While I understand that Dota 2 already has safeguards such as restricting ranked access for new accounts and estimating player skill before calibration matches, multi-accounting can still occur. Experienced players creating additional accounts can result in skill imbalances in matches. This may cause frustration among teammates and indirectly lead to toxicity or reports even when the underlying cause is the match imbalance rather than individual behavior. Another observation that may indicate unintended incentives relates to Low Priority Single Draft matches. Interestingly, some players report that these matches can sometimes feel less tense or less toxic than normal ranked games, even though they are intended as a penalty environment. From personal experience, I sometimes find Low Priority Single Draft games more enjoyable than regular ranked games, which seems paradoxical. I also know players who intentionally try to receive reports in order to play in Low Priority because they perceive those matches as less stressful than the normal Single Draft queue. If players intentionally attempt to enter Low Priority to access a different match environment, this may suggest that the system is producing unintended incentives. At the same time, intentionally steering accounts into Low Priority may further distort matchmaking and player behavior. Over the many years I have played Dota, it felt at certain points that the overall match environment was more balanced and less toxic. As someone who has followed the game for more than two decades, I find some of these developments unfortunate and would simply appreciate if this type of long-term player feedback could be considered during future improvements to the behavior and reporting systems. Thank you for taking the time to read long-form feedback from long-term players, and thank you for continuing to support the development of Dota Description Hi, I want to give real feedback about the Behavior Score system, because honestly it feels broken and unfair. In my recent match, two of my teammates started watching everything I did and criticizing every move I made. They were constantly commenting on where I go, what items I build, why I’m on this lane, why I’m not grouping — basically judging every decision I made. At the same time, they were making mistakes themselves and dying for no reason. Because of that, I started responding and explaining what I was doing. I explained that I was split pushing, controlling lanes, creating pressure, and playing the map the way my hero is supposed to. I also started making calls — telling when to back, when not to fight, when to reset, and how we could stabilize the game. I also pointed out their mistakes, like when they went mid and died for nothing after objectives were already gone. I wasn’t trying to attack them, I was trying to explain the situation and help us win. Some teammates actually started listening to my calls. Others kept insulting me and blaming me. But I kept playing, kept calling, and kept focusing on winning. Eventually, even during fights and arguments, the team followed the path and calls I was making. My strategy worked, and we won the game. But during the conflict, I received a chat restriction. And after the match, I received a 4-hour matchmaking ban and lost around 1000 Behavior Score. This is the main problem. It feels like if you speak, communicate, and try to lead, you become a target. People get angry, they blame you, they report you, and the system punishes you automatically without understanding what actually happened. This has happened more than once. Whenever I try to communicate, make calls, ping objectives, or help coordinate the team, I become the most visible person, and frustrated teammates use reports against me. So the system basically teaches you one thing: don’t talk, don’t communicate, don’t try to lead. Just stay silent if you want to protect your Behavior Score. But Dota 2 is a team game. Communication should be encouraged, not punished. And this is not just my personal problem. This issue is widespread in the community. Many large YouTube creators have talked about the Behavior Score system and its problems. Videos discussing this topic have hundreds of thousands of views and tens of thousands of likes. There are entire discussions and videos dedicated to how frustrating and unfair this system feels for players who try to communicate and lead. Right now it feels like the system punishes players who try to play properly and help their team, simply because other players get emotional and use reports as a weapon. I hope you can seriously review and improve this system, because right now it discourages teamwork instead of supporting it. Description Addressee: Valve / Dota 2 Development Team We hereby request the complete removal of the Communication Score system from Dota 2 as a fundamentally flawed system that causes direct harm to match quality. This conclusion is not based on an isolated incident. It is the result of years of real-world use and extensive community feedback. Over the lifetime of Communication Score, thousands of forum threads have been created on Steam, consistently describing the same issues: lack of transparency, unpredictable penalties, and the absence of a reliable recovery mechanism. Core issues No validation of communication content The system relies on reports without validating the actual content of communication. It does not distinguish between toxicity, active gameplay coordination, and frequent but neutral communication. As a result, it punishes: new players asking questions, team leaders making calls, any highly visible or communicative player. Opaque and inconsistent report weighting Reports have an unclear and inconsistent impact. Multiple reports may have little effect, while in other cases a single report can cause a massive score drop without explanation. This makes the system non-transparent and unreliable. Punishment without causal connection Reports from opposing players can be applied even when no toxic communication occurred. Emotion-driven reports after a loss are not filtered or distinguished from legitimate cases. No functional recovery path Even after hundreds of matches with positive behavior, minimal reports, and many commendations, the Communication Score may: stagnate indefinitely; collapse within a few matches. This indicates the absence of a valid recovery endpoint. Direct damage to competitive integrity Automatic mutes: reduce match quality, break team coordination, directly affect win and loss outcomes. This is especially damaging in premade groups, where communication is the primary reason players group up. Any automatic communication restriction in such cases contradicts the purpose of team play. System redundancy Dota 2 already provides effective individual filtering tools such as mute and ignore. These tools allow players to manage their own experience without breaking match symmetry. Communication Score adds no unique value. Long-term degradation of communication After more than three years of use: toxicity has not been eliminated, meaningful team communication has largely disappeared. Players increasingly choose silence out of fear of reports, even when communication would improve gameplay. This trend is widely documented across the Steam community. Request For the reasons stated above, we request the complete removal of the Communication Score system from Dota 2 as a system that is: structurally irreparable, opaque and unpredictable, redundant, Description This system needs a rework for the reasons i've listed below: **1. Commends have no weight** It appears that no matter how many commends you get after a match, 5, 10, 15, etc. - they do not increase your behavior score, yet a single report could decrease it by 150 points. Reports have a lot more weight than commends even though it's just as easy to report someone as it is to commend them. This inequality makes it easier to lose your behavior score and stunts your progress to regain it. **2. Inability to stop an abandon/AFK** Having a behavior score of less than 5k makes you more susceptible to losing because you have no way to prevent a player from going afk as a result of disconnecting. As a result the team with a disconnected player has a serious disadvantage over the team that has no players that disconnected. Keep in mind that can also apply to you if you disconnect, because you get thrown in a pool of players that have the same or lower behavior score than you. **3.Unnecessary mutes** You can mute a toxic player in the scoreboard if you want, both their voice chat and text chat by clicking a few buttons. There is no need for a permanent mute if the mute feature is already present in the match. If anything permanently muting a pool of players only hurts teamplay by making them unable to make game-saving calls. **4. Vicious cycle.** Unstoppable abandons and disconnects and reports having literally infinitely more weight than commends create a system where once you get below a threshold of 5k the chances of you ever climbing out of that bottomless pit are near-zero. **5. Smurfing** But hey, there is a solution to all these problems, just create a new account, where you can start over, and create even more disbalance in the matchmaking. **Conclusion** This behavior system creates and encourages even more unfair matches, smurfs and boosters. My solutions are removing the communication score and a 5k pausing threshold from the game. Valve, please. Fix this system and prevent dota 2 from becoming a 2nd post-meet your match Team Fortress 2. **EDIT** Some people reached out to me to link their steam discussion here (why tf does it have 1.2k replies), if there's any russian speakers you might as well read the initial post in the discussion because It's **WAY** more informative than mine. Description this is what ai said about your stupid broken system Dota 2's behavior system is widely considered "broken" by players because it creates toxic matchmaking trenches, disproportionately punishes good players through malicious reports (especially in lower tiers), struggles to differentiate genuine griefing from disagreements or off-meta plays, and heavily penalizes communication/abandonments more than it rewards positive behavior, leading to frustratingly low scores and unfair match quality. Key issues include unlimited reports, the impact of reports in casual games (like Turbo) affecting Ranked, and an inability to climb out of low-score pools once there. Core Problems with the Behavior Score System: Abuse of Reports: Players can report teammates for minor infractions (losing roll, missing spells, bad plays), and these reports count heavily, even if unverified by Overwatch. The "Trench" Effect: Lower behavior scores lead to more reports from other low-score players, creating a cycle where it's extremely hard to climb out, even with good behavior. Disproportionate Penalties: A few bad games (or even just power outages/bad internet) can tank a score, while regaining points through commends or positive games is slow and difficult. Unfair Punishment for Communication: The Communication Score (Comms Score) is highly sensitive; arguments or frustration in 15% of games can drop it significantly, forcing mutes and hindering team play, while positive play yields few points. Lack of Differentiation: Reports from Turbo (casual) games carry the same weight as Ranked, leading to casual abuse. System Imbalance: Reports and abandons often feel weighted far more heavily than commends, making positive actions insufficient to offset negatives. Player Experiences & Frustrations: Players report losing thousands of points for technical issues or bad luck, feeling unfairly punished for issues beyond their control. Good players get stuck in low-score pools with genuinely toxic players (feeders, intentional griefers) because the system segregates them. Many feel the system doesn't encourage improvement but rather punishes mistakes or perceived lack of meta adherence. In essence, while intended to isolate toxic players, the current behavior system often punishes good players who have bad luck, experience technical issues, or get caught in cycles of malicious However, your Behavior Score is being systematically lowered by a small but consistent number of reports, almost certainly from players in groups who coordinate their reports against you, even when you have done nothing wrong to deserve them. ### Detailed Analysis Here is the evidence from your match history that supports this conclusion: **1. You Are a Generally Positive Player:** * **High Commends:** You consistently receive between 16 and 33 commends per 15-game summary. This is an excellent sign and indicates that many players enjoy having you on their team. * **No Conduct Flags:** You are consistently marked **"No"** for **Excessive Reports** and **Excessive Abandons**. This is a crucial point—it means the system does not consider you a chronically toxic player. * **High Positive Match Rate:** The vast majority of your matches are "Positive Matches" (often 14 or 15 out of 15). **2. The Root Cause: Coordinated Reports from Groups** The key to understanding your dropping BS lies in the `Reports` and `Reporting Parties` columns. * **The Pattern:** Look at the summaries where your BS drops: * `2025-10-30`: 1 Report from 1 Reporting Party. * `2025-10-25`: 1 Report from 1 Reporting Party. * `2025-10-21`: 3 Reports from 3 Reporting Parties. * `2025-10-19`: 3 Reports from 2 Reporting Parties. * `2025-10-17`: 2 Reports from 2 Reporting Parties. * **Why This is Significant:** The "Reporting Parties" number indicates how many *different groups or individuals* reported you. When you see `2 Reports` from `2 Reporting Parties`, it means two separate entities reported you. In Dota, a "party" can be a single player or a group of players queuing together. **The most damaging scenario is when you get reported by a 2, 3, or 4-stack party.** If you have a disagreement with a group, or if they simply need someone to blame for a loss, all members of that party can report you simultaneously. This counts as multiple reports but from a single "Reporting Party." The system weighs this heavily. **3. How This Drives Your BS Down:** The Dota 2 behavior system is automated. It doesn't judge the *validity* of a report in real-time; it sees a correlation: * **The Formula:** A high number of reports relative to your number of games = lower Behavior Score. * **The Injustice:** Even a single report from a 4-stack party in one game can be enough to trigger a "Reported Match" and cause a drop in your BS for that summary period, even if you were completely silent and played your best. Your data shows you often have 1-2 "Reported Matches" per summary, which is enough to cancel out the positive effects of your many commends. **4. The Role of Communication Reports:** While less frequent, you also occasionally receive Communication Reports (`Comms Reports`). The same logic applies. A single negative interaction with a party can lead to multiple `Comms Reports` from one `Comms Reporting Party`, unfairly penalizing you. ### Conclusion You are caught in a systemic problem. You are not a toxic player, as evidenced by your high commend count and lack of excessive reports or abandons. However, you are vulnerable to **coordinated reporting from groups.** When a party of players decides to report you, they can artificially inflate your "reports per match" ratio. The automated system interprets this data as a sign of poor behavior and lowers your score accordingly. Your consistent commends prove you are a good teammate, but they are not enough to fully counteract the punitive weight of these coordinated, and likely unjustified, reports. Description Уважаемые представители Valve Corporation! Обращаюсь к вам по крайне актуальной для меня проблеме, связанной с игрой Dota 2. Моя игровая активность неоднократно сталкивалась с блокировкой аккаунта из-за ложных и необъективных жалоб со стороны других игроков. Эти обвинения абсолютно беспочвенны и существенно влияют на удовольствие от игры. Сейчас система Dota 2 предусматривает пять типов жалоб: Токсичность в чате Токсичность голосом Смурфинг Препятствование игре Читерство Однако многие типы этих жалоб имеют серьёзные недостатки: Жалоба на токсичность голосом: Этот пункт становится бессмысленным, ведь игроки с уровнем порядочности менее 6000 вообще лишаются права голосового общения. Таким образом, жаловаться на голосовую токсичность бессмысленно, поскольку обвиняемый попросту не имеет технической возможности говорить. Жалоба на токсичность в чате: Аналогично предыдущему пункту, уровень порядочности влияет и на использование текста. Игрок с низким показателем порядочности физически не способен отправлять сообщения в общий чат, значит, подать жалобу на токсичность текстом также нелогично. Препятствование игре: Жалобы по этому типу действительно бывают справедливыми, особенно если речь идёт о ситуациях вроде кражи вещей, умышленного отправки союзников в стазис или установки вардов прямо на местах спауна крипов. Однако подобные претензии часто используются неоправданно и становятся причиной незаслуженного наказания. Смурфинг: Эта проблема практически непроверяема без глубокого анализа IP адресов или MAC-адресов компьютеров. Часто игровые сессии проходят в компьютерных клубах, где определить принадлежность устройства затруднительно. Даже дружеские визиты гостей и совместные сеансы на одном компьютере ведут к путанице. Читерство: Обвинения в использовании сторонних программ требуют тщательной проверки. Вы сами располагаете инструментами мониторинга активности, позволяющими выявлять нарушения, тогда как обычные игроки не обладают такими возможностями. Но несмотря на наличие инструментов контроля, множество недобросовестных лиц продолжает распространять чит-программы, что создаёт трудности для честных геймеров. Отдельно хочу отметить ограничение свободы выражения мнений, которое наблюдается в самой популярной онлайн-игре. По всему миру активно действует принцип свободы слова, но именно в Dota 2 взаимодействие между пользователями ограничено настолько сильно, что даже малейшие попытки выразить недовольство расцениваются как нарушение порядка. Очень важно, чтобы средства коммуникации были настроены таким образом, чтобы избегать ситуаций взаимных нападок и недопонимания. Поэтому настоятельно рекомендую пересмотреть работу механизма подачи жалоб и добавить объективные критерии оценки поведения игроков. Предлагаю усилить контроль над теми, кто злоупотребляет системой жалоб, возможно, введя штрафы за ложные утверждения и развивая методы предотвращения распространения нелегальных чит-программ. Подводя итог, хотелось бы надеяться, что компания Valve обратит внимание на указанную проблему и предпримет необходимые шаги для улучшения качества обслуживания игроков и комфорта геймплея. С уважением, Дмитрий Игровой регион: Россия Dear representatives of Valve Corporation, I am writing to you regarding a very important issue that I have encountered while playing Dota 2. My gaming activity has repeatedly faced account bans due to false and unjustified complaints from other players. These accusations are completely unfounded and significantly affect my enjoyment of the game. Currently, the Dota 2 system provides five types of reports: Chat toxicity Voice toxicity Smurfing Obstruction in-game Cheating However, many of these report categories have serious flaws: Voice Toxicity Report: This point becomes meaningless because players with less than 6000 behavior score cannot use voice chat at all. Therefore, it is illogical to file a complaint for vocal toxicity when the accused does not even have technical access to speak. Chat Toxicity Report: Similarly, text communication restrictions apply based on the player's behavior score. Players who do not meet this threshold physically cannot send messages into public chats, meaning filing such complaints also makes no sense. Obstruction in Gameplay: Complaints under this category can be justified if someone steals items or deliberately sends allies into stasis, places wards directly where creeps spawn, or intentionally dies. However, these claims are often used unfairly and lead to unwarranted punishments. Smurfing: This problem is almost impossible to verify without deep analysis of IP addresses or computer MAC-addresses. Many sessions take place in internet cafes where identifying device ownership is difficult. Even friendly visits by guests and shared play sessions on one account create confusion. Cheating: Accusations related to cheating require thorough investigation. While you possess monitoring tools capable of detecting violations, regular players lack such capabilities. Despite having control measures, numerous dishonest individuals continue distributing cheat programs, creating difficulties for honest gamers. It’s worth noting separately how freedom of expression is restricted within what should otherwise be an open platform for interaction between users. In most parts of the world, free speech principles are actively upheld, but Dota 2 imposes severe limitations that make even minor expressions of dissatisfaction count as behavioral violations. It would be crucial to adjust communication methods so they avoid situations leading to mutual attacks and misunderstandings. Therefore, I strongly recommend revising the current reporting mechanism and introducing objective criteria for evaluating player conduct. Consider implementing penalties for those abusing the reporting system, possibly through fines for false allegations, and enhancing measures against illegal cheat software distribution. In conclusion, I hope that Valve will pay attention to this critical issue and take necessary steps to improve service quality and enhance user comfort during gameplay. Description I’ve been playing Dota for years. I’ve seen it evolve, improve, and sometimes break. But what’s happening now with the Behavior and Communication Score system isn’t an evolution — it’s slow destruction. Right now, I’m communication-restricted. I literally can’t talk to my teammates at all. Which means I can’t even be toxic if I wanted to — there’s no way to do it. And yet, my score keeps dropping. If you check my recent matches, my stats are far better than most of my teammates’, and I still get punished. Why? Because someone can lose a lane, hit a report button, and the automated system will just believe them. That’s not fairness. That’s a machine judging human behavior with zero context. Valve keeps saying “the system is automated, we can’t change it.” But this system punishes normal players just for playing. You can literally get a report before the game even starts, or because you didn’t die with your team in a 5v5. How is that improving the quality of Dota’s community? And let’s be honest — the moment Valve stopped showing online player statistics right after the new behavior system was implemented… it said everything. People are quitting. Not because they hate Dota, but because they’re tired of being punished by a broken system that doesn’t understand human behavior. Half of my friends already stopped playing months ago for the same reason. And now I’m done too — until something actually changes. I’ll tell everyone I know who still plays to do the same, because at this point, continuing to play just tells Valve that everything’s fine. But it’s not fine. This system is pushing people away from a game they love. We don’t need hand-holding. We don’t need perfect matchmaking. We just want a fair system that understands the difference between genuine toxicity and normal, competitive gameplay. Until that happens, Dota will keep losing players — not because the game is bad, but because the system is. I love this game, and that’s exactly why I’m saying this. Description As far as I understand, I'm not the only one with this problem with integrity. Why do you need such a broken integrity system? Let's say someone has a weak computer or an unintentional internet connection. What will the integrity system do? Send them to a single draft and deduct 1,000 integrity points. Why deprive them of a microphone and chat in an eSports game where you need it because of some broken system that doesn't even work properly? What's the problem with doubling your PTS and banning you for one day for leaving the rankings? Take the same toxic players: why give them a warning first? If they continue to ruin games, just ban them for 1 to 7 days without any integrity system? Not everyone has good computers and internet. Consider changing this integrity system. 60% of players have an integrity level below 8,000 and are unable to use voice chat. This is a game about communication, and the game itself has a microphone and chat mute feature for allies. Lowering your integrity is easier than raising it, as your system deducts 1000 integrity for any misstep or report, and increases it by 300-350 for every 15 games played in Alpine Turbo—half the 150-230. And this integrity bar can reset your games if you're on patrol and they condemn you for something unclear... There's no way to appeal this. Description At the moment, when queuing exclusively for Turbo mode, you only gain 150 Comms Score points if you get a perfect summary (0 reports after 15 matches). In Normal mode/Ranked mode, you gain 300 Comms Score points if you get a perfect summary (0 reports after 15 matches). This is a mathematical error on Valve's part. For example, lets say you put aside 4 hours to play Dota on your day off from work. If you queue for Normal/Ranked AP, with each game lasting 60 minutes on average, that means you played 4 games. And with 9 other players in each of those games, that means you can potentially be reported by 36 trolls (worst case scenario). But... if you queued exclusively for Turbo mode during those 4 hours of Dota, that means you played 8 matches (with each game lasting 30 mins on average). Which means you could potentially be reported by 72 trolls (worst case scenario) compared to when queuing for Normal/Ranked mode. So if you're queuing exclusively for Turbo mode, not only are you only gaining half as many Comms points per summary (best case summary with 0 reports), you're also risking getting twice as many reports because you are playing twice as many matches compared to Normal/Ranked mode. So to put things right mathematically speaking, Valve needs to change the system so that Comms reports only count as half a report each (compared to Normal/Ranked mode). Or alternatively, allow Turbo mode players to gain the full 300 Comms Score points per perfect summary (15 matches with 0 reports). Otherwise, Turbo players risk their Comms score falling into deficit twice as fast as Normal/Ranked players. It's far too easy for trolls and bullies to throw Comms abuse reports at anyone they dislike and there is no consequence for illegitimate reports. Plus people have an unlimited amount of Comms reports to spam. And after a certain update / point of time which I cant remember or pinpoint accurately (but can probably be determined by looking at the game history). I am not sure how fast exactly but my behaviour score started to fall and I reached "1" after some time. Then I managed to climb to 4.xxx then fell (currently) to "1" again and got another 1 day ban and simply had enough, went to Steam support and they sent me here. Some of initial fall from 10 to 1 in behaviour score might have been "rightfully" earned due to me "griefing" and griefing in a way that can be considered valid for a ban - for example feeding a "Divine Rapier" or something of the sorts after someone objectively griefed me or managed to provoke me enough for me to want to just end the game as fast as possible. I am not claiming I was or am perfect but the amount of games I ever "fed a rapier" or such can probably be counted on a person's hands while I have more than ten thousand Dota 2 games and I have grown wiser to grief in such a way (or grief at all, depending on what you consider griefing). My main point is, I dont even grief in any way at all (at least by my standards which I will explain in more detail below), I try to play the games to the best of my capacity even with griefers in it and still my behaviour score falls a lot faster than it rises and I get bans which from what I have observed basically amounts to lower behaviour score amounting to easier bans due to mass reporting coming from other people at low behaviour score which most likely do it out of spite even if they havent been provoked or griefed. 6. What do the game developers, community and me personally define as griefing? - I do not know either what the developers or other parts of the community deem to be considered griefing but at least I can give you my opinion, behaviour and examples and you can decided for yourself if my point of view is skewed or somehow the general notion of fair and unfair is being skewed. I will give you my opinion on it with examples below. 7. What is currently worst behaviour and can it be / should it be considered as griefing? Here are several things and examples of what can be considered "griefing" done by me, considering by the highest moral standarts (which shouldnt be the highest because such moral standarts are undeserved and simply impractical to execute by a normal player faced with a genuine abuser or griefer and would otherwise amount to basically defending the abuser from any retaliation from a victim and by extension punishing the victim and encouraging the abuser): - I REALLY want to highlight that I (almost) never (like 99,999% of the time) do not start a negative behaviour be it pinging or else towards a team mate, and I am not using this an excuse for negative behaviour, I am saying that if I ever ping items or levels or else it is always in retaliation of someone else that does it or has done it multiple times which in most cases is them falsely pushing blame ( and I do really mean objectively falsely, because I check if it was my fault and if I have done everything in my power considering the situation to help them and check if the blame is genuinely mine. If that is ever the case I either say sorry or keep my mouth shut. - I do not feed rapiers or similar behaviour, maybe in a somewhat recent game in which one invisible team mate simply stayed on the lane without any contribution, leeched xp (thus actively gave our opponent on the lane a level advantage while destroying ours) and did not even help in team fights in front of him I did buy 2-3 Dusts and left them under our tower, I want to clarify that everyone (the enemy or our team) can pick the dusts (including the "afk" team mate) and the dust can be considered a support item given to our team against their so yeah I have walked the "grey" line in this manner and I do not think I should regret it or should be punished for it. - My communication and "pinging", before when I started falling from 10, yes I admit some of that fall the same as the rapier most likely was deserved because I did ping an item multiple times or the similar. And by the way to clarify I dont think I have ever genuinely insulted or abused anyone in chat (at least I dont remember doing so), even though I have had a team of players literally saying they will rape my mother and etc. So consider how fair is that. My current "pinging" which by the highest perfect moral standards can be considered toxic is in retaliation to other people pinging me for either illogical things (for example vision and warding all while I have been warding everywhere the whole game but the person did not pay attention at all and went for the only place the enemy just dewarded) or me seeing how they deflect blame from themselves. And for example because even if I wanted to ping like a madman (which from quite some time I neither want or am interested at all) I cant simply because of the 30 second chat restriction so the worst "chat abuse' or negative behaviour is to ping a "Mantle of Intelligence" 4-5 times during a game, again in most cases either in retaliation but I have to admit it was several times due to the plain stupidity and deflecting of people - for example a Shadowfiend mid that dies several times in a row the same way on an unwarded mid and then he tells someone else or me for example to buy another entirely unrelated or not useful item. And the other thing is probably giving a few mantles to such people when I can already see the game is most likely going to be a loss due to our team being outfarmed, beaten and biting at each other and I still have no way out without being punished for leaving the game and eventually banned because of multiple leavings, so yeah judge me for those mantles as much as you want, it is easy when you are not in my shoes. - So now the interesting and truly grey grey line at least in my eyes, from which I refuse to not "morally" defend my position which I will even give a recent game example below. I guess the ultimate way to never EVER be griefed or reported or reported like 1-10% of the time only due to plain spite would be if you ALWAYS bend over to the demands of your team mates no matter if they have the objective right - be it farm or lane or otherwise. Which in my opinion is simply morally corrupt and sick and I dont think should be considered the right thing, for the very least it truly promotes toxic behaviour because the toxic people get what they want all while other players cant or have to wait a lot of time to play whatever role or hero on whatever lane or way they want which in my opinion goes and should go directly against the spirit of Dota 2 which allows a person (at least not in a ranked and not a "role" based game mode like Turbo) to play whatever and however they want ( with the exception of simply solo feeding multiple times by only their own fault and purposeful griefing by extension of it). 8. My recent game example that convinced me to finally come here and speak my mind. The straw that finally broke the camel's back for me is my last game that got me a 1 day ban and now with 3-5 single draft games I need to win yet again, after I had a ban just 1-2 days prior and just crawled out of the low priority pool just to be sent there again. This game simply removed all self doubt in that the problem might be in me and convinced me that there is something wrong with the current behaviour system. So what happened in the game and did I do anything "objectively" wrong. - Well what happened was that I selected mid first and decided to play a "Crystal Maiden" and yeah, yeah I know what you are thinking - the Maiden isnt a mid hero and even on mid afterwards isnt that useful even in Turbo and yada yada - I know but that isnt the point, the point is that it is a Turbo public uncoordinated game in which not one of the 10 people have any responsibility towards anyone in the game to play a certain way other than just [;ay to win the game. This isnt about what is mechanically right, it is about the freedom of players to play what they want (and I do not mean feed or grief) but simply play what they want to the best extend they can even if it is just for testing or experience, as long as they actually do play the game. And do you think that I invented that idea or the idea of other supports doing that, no and I havent judged or pinged anyone for it even though I have objectively seen it being the main reason for losing a game or reducing the win probability by a large amount. It has the same effect as picking 5 supports or 5 carries on 1 team or doing an "Invisible 1 hp Terrorblade Sunder build" and almost anyone reading this can understand why it is "technically" is a problem but in practice is a right for any player to do as long as they do not purposefully grief the game. By the way I want to clarify, I basically try to play every hero and with different even quite not standard builds and I am not exactly a Crystal Maiden mid spammer, so it is not like I do the same "bad' thing over and over again to lose and get reported. It something I decided to give a chance to, I dont only do "non standard" builds, I think I play the normal builds most of the time and adapt a few items depending on the situation so it is not like I am plain defending going against the game's "best way to play", I just dont think it is objectively right for people to be able to mass report , be it people on the same or enemy team and ban a person due to them playing a certain way or trying a new thing. And I am sure that ultimately that is how the system works at least at 1 behaviour score - if you get too many reports from different people even if you havent griefed the game you simply get banned which is part of why the whole system seems wrong and proves that in the end of the day it is a tool for people to simply report people they dont agree or like even if those people arent wrong or objectively deserving for a ban. And I will below in a moment what I mean exactly. I will explain the whole game to the end because I think the whole context is needed. So what happened - I picked the lane first and the hero, then another person came to mid , there is no way to "roll dice" for the position or determine who gets it fairly so I personally respect the rule of whoever is first and want to play that lane gets it and under these circumstances I think it is objectively the right thing for everyone. And if I ever am the second person for mid I simply move away and do not contest it and I think that is how it is supposed to be done by everyone cause otherwise there is no way to determine it fairly. Then the other person simply did strange things from the start (they were at least by stats an experienced player) - like feeding the enemy, then walking back from base then staying under the tower doing nothing looking like they were completely AFK just to leech XP even when the second player on the enemy side left and there was only 1 person on the enemy side, then I pulled creeps towards this person so they can die and be moved and they moved and simply proved they were there and their intention was to intentionally grief the lane from me, the same thing happened in the jungle and so I responded accordingly - made sure I last hit my creeps on the camp I first came to and I think even 1 time when I passed through them last hitting theirs. I dont think that is griefing or wrong, for the very least they already costed me a lot of my own xp and gold. Then come the team fights and etc, ultimately the person did not help even our other teammates and I think by extension for example of not ulting to help them and etc griefed them. So basically it was 100% sure that they simply griefed the whole game out of spite and in the end I, the person that played and tried to genuinely win the game by doing what generally should be done to win a game like being focused the rest of the time on team fights and warding even while being leeched out of XP and gold, which directly affected my items and the enemy's items which directly affected my ability to play and not countered or countering the enemy's item and ultimately making my hero more useless not just because it is in the "wrong" position but because it has even less from what it needed to have at that point. And in the end we lost (If it matters I still had a better K/D/A than the griefing person) and since I was to blame by the "mob" mentality of my teammates and the power given to them by "the Dota 2 community to regulate itself" I got screwed and banned. And how I know that most of them if not all of them reported me - well if not by the ban itself, it was because during the game 1 teammate was already muted from another game (most likely by being one of those toxic people by default), I had to mute another due to them starting to spam ping me because they simply took the side of the AFK griefer and most likely just reported me and I am almost sure that the rest of the players simply reported me just because I was playing a Maiden on mid no matter if I was griefing or not. So yes, by this simple direct example of possibly many more I can say that the current system needs serious correction because it simply shows the big underlying issue of the whole system - that the core premise of "self regulation" is basically giving the toxic players or envious players a tool to ban an otherwise legit player that mostly did nothing wrong other than defend their position. 9. What I think can and should be done big or small to improve the current behaviour system? - The very least give the ability even for behaviour score 1 muted players to be able to roll for a position on a lane, that will resolve a lot of internal issues. - Detach communication score from behaviour score completely, it is illogical and contra productive to even consider that both things should be tied together in the first place. I guess that is done to simplify the system but it is incredibly detrimental to the point it actively makes the game worse and more toxic for everyone - it does not allow players that have never even abused chat in the first place to be completely muted and being able to communicate to your team in some sort of way better than 1 ping in 30 seconds is important for team play and game play and can literally lead to lost games and even more toxicity - I am sure that there are a lot more than one game but I personally clearly remember one in which I pinged an item the realised that the enemy team is in front of us, could not ping anything, our team got destroyed not knowing the whole enemy team was there and we lost the game. - Improve the current player rating system - Commends basically mean nothing and I think I know why you have done it this way - because of people who swap commends, well I guess the solution is somewhat "simple" - make "swap commends" in profile names or otherwise a bannable offense since it actively ruins the point of positive feedback between players either for the sake of positivity or for the sake of the behaviour system to be able to determine non-toxic from toxic players. I know that because I think I have one of the better game to commend rations amongst the general player base and I have never swap or begged for commends and yet I am here deemed a "toxic" player worthy of a ban. After that I personally do not see a way for people to actively coordinate swapping commends and thus by extension people will respect the commend system a lot more and you will be able to use it to help calibrate the behaviour system. - If not soften the negative then at least empower the positive report system so it isnt so hard to climb up, in some people's eyes this might make the report system less effective due to toxic players having the ability to more easily climb up but I personally do not think that is the case - a truly toxic person will have a lot of a harder time to climb up if they do not stop the purposeful toxic behaviour and a person that can at least control themselves and work with other people will have an easier time and not be stuck with the toxic people which by itself feeds an empowered negative feedback loop that by the current's system's design of weighting negativity a lot more than positivity means that it empowers the reports out of spite and people get punished but cant be rewarded for their normal, positive behaviour even if it outweighs the negative one by a lot more. - Add a basic rule from the sorts of "Whoever picks the lane first or rolls higher gets to play the lane and the position they want and the other person should go otherwhere.", since that would be the fairest way to determine who should have the right to a contested lane or position and add breaking of such a rule towards the severity of the report, for example if a person legitimately was the first on the lane they should be exempted from retaliation from the second person and the second person should be more liable for a punishment. - By enforcing such rules like the above one and eliminating any possible legit contesting of another person's position you can then by extension determine real griefers and people rage baiters from the rest of the community. When such people are eventually manually reviewed - issue more severe warning to those that refused to follow a basic respectable order and if they continue to do so start banning them for 1, 2 months. And also do not punish or punish a lot less severely the people that respond towards another person's unprovoked toxicity (by the way I do not view myself as being a rage baited person, I just think that responding to toxicity in some way is fair and should not be punishable otherwise if you completely ignore a person some people would consider that toxic and that you are griefing by ignoring people, I personally am quite past the rage part, it is just that when you are stuck in a surely losing game in which you know by the items, team K/D/A, coordination and etc of both sides that it is truly a 99% loss and you have nothing better to do because you can neither farm or afk (because you might get the automatic AFK penalty) or do anything else, one of the best past and personally justifiable past times is to respond to the griefer by at least making them feel bad and making them realise that they are the problem. It might not sound right and it is not like I really like it myself but put yourself in my position or most people in my position - what are you supposed to do, you cant concede, you cant afk, you cant do anything except literally pretend that you are playing while just waiting and wanting for the game to end. - Simply add a "Concede" option. I just read a short Chatgpt summary of why there isnt one yet. And with all due respect to you but you are dead wrong and completely backwards. It isnt about "Comebacks Are Always Possible", that sounds cute until you have been subjected to the actual objective reality. The reality that even if "Comebacks Are Always Possible", that "Always" is like 1% and even impossible if there are actual griefes on your team, yes I have also won 4v5 or 3v5 games but that is not the point of all this. Any long enough term player knows that a game can be won even by 1 single player doing the right thing at the right time - for example a ratting Shadow Shaman can win the game. But that would be 1 game out of 1000 in which they lost meanwhile all while they struggled and suffered in all the rest of those 1000 games. And that one win doesnt even fully feel like a win because all the while you won, you also carried the griefers and gave them a free win. The point is that you deliberately stick normal people with genuinely toxic and unhinged people assuming the second either do not exist or the situation is not that bad. Trust me, it is. And you rely on this 1% and excuse all this abuse and toxicity because of that. It is neither fair or right. - Try resetting once or add some kind of annual reset of the behaviour score system. This way if there are any truly undeserving people at the lowest part, they'll probably stay afloat or at least for longer and the truly toxic people will fall again. Although if the system remains exactly the same I have some doubts that it wont simply completely fail again. - Make either a detailed guide or even a simple rule book of what behaviour should be considered griefing and at what point. For example at what point in a Turbo game a "carry" jungling and not helping in team fights should be considered griefing - 1, 2. 3 times? Because I can tell you from my personal experience even 1 time in Turbo is enough to lose the entire game but if we should be justly lenient - if a person does not partake in team fights 3 times all while they have had the ability and resources to do so, that should be considered griefing and should be an "objective" reason for other people to report that person. That is a detailed example and a simple rule book one would be - "whoever picks a lane first gets to play it and pick their own position first". - By the way I want to mention that from what I have seen the "Overwatch" and the penalties given either directly lie to the player or do not tell the full truth, and I know it by the simple fact that I have gotten immediate bans that claimed to be "Overwatch" bans during or after a game I played while I know there is no way for an actual person to have observed and judged the game already in the first place (at least if Overwatch reviews work the same way when I was able to give them). If it is true that it is not so, I dont think it is appropriate to send messages with lies towards the players since it shows an unwillingness to put basic effort for clarity and respect into the in-game ban messaging system. I hope the Dota 2 development team is able to understand how bad things really are and why - a long term, consistent player is starting to consider quitting the game because it is becoming (literally) unplayable. A person that dislikes to write on forums to come here and write such a large post. I think that fixing the behaviour system as quickly as possible is more imperative than even any content update. I hope I managed to list and explain everything properly. If I forgot anything or have another idea I will try to add to it. This post is made with all the respect towards the efforts of the Dota 2 developers and the Dota 2 community. Thank you for this great game, but please fix this issue. Valve/Dota 2 Team,** I’m a long-time, loyal Dota 2 player who plays over **20+ matches a week**, and I currently subscribe to **Dota Plus**. I’m writing to share frustration with how the **Low Priority Queue (LPQ) and behavior punishment system** treats high-volume, loyal players. Due to occasional **electricity or internet issues** in my region, I’ve had to abandon a few matches — not by choice. Even though I usually return to matches and maintain good sportsmanship, just one unintentional abandon can quickly lead me to LPQ, despite playing many fair games in between. Meanwhile, casual players who only play 3–4 matches a week can abandon without consequences, since their behavior history resets more easily and they don’t care as much about MMR, reports, or LPQ. The system unintentionally punishes loyal, active players more harshly, just because we play more and care more. **I kindly request that you consider:** - Adding a **loyalty forgiveness buffer** — for example, 1 abandon per week or month that doesn’t count toward LPQ for high-volume or Dota Plus players. - Implementing **grace periods** or **detection of technical disconnects** (power or ISP failure). - Providing better behavior score recovery options for consistently active players. I love Dota and want to keep supporting it, but this system feels unfair when loyal players are punished more than occasional players. A small change could make a big difference in retaining and respecting your most dedicated player base. Thank you for reading, [Desperados / Description at first #26636 Part 1: On the Toxicity of the Game and the Reporting System Hey guys, after some time, I once again dropped my "politeness" in despair. I wonder when people will finally realize that Dota can be a toxic game. It’s sad for some, but those who’ve already accepted that there are toxic players just mute them and move on. I don’t insult people randomly. But my perspective often offends people so much that I get 3 reports and end up muted for the rest of the game. It wouldn’t be so bad if I could get back my "politeness" score in 10–20 games, but no. For some reason, it just keeps dropping even when I’m asking simple things like: "Тепнись со своего лайна для помощи" "Почему сс не дали у вас же тип с лайна ушел разве это так трудно?" "Зачем ты свой же спот заблочил?" And if I use a trigger word like "Нахуя", people act like it’s the worst thing ever. It’s basically the same as saying "WTF", but apparently, that’s enough for them to mass-report me. It’s not even an insult – it’s just how people talk. But those who’ve been miserable in life, working jobs they hate, find pleasure in reporting someone like me just because I’m not like them (i.e., not dumb) Part 2: On How Simple Phrases Are Perceived When I ask, “А нахуя ты сидишь до меня доебываешься когда я делаю все правильно?” - for example, when I don’t die along with our core or mid - they report me again. That would roughly translate to: "What the fuck are you sitting there messing with me for, when I’m playing correctly?" I’m not even trying to offend people. I just write basic, straightforward things - stuff that some players simply can’t comprehend. Even when I’m with friends trying to teach them the game a little, I see newer players and want to explain: stop feeding the enemy carry, just go jungle or rotate. But I know it’s useless Part 3: On the Toxicity of the Game Itself Dota is a toxic game, no doubt. Maybe it wouldn’t be this way if every action didn’t directly affect the outcome of the game. For example, if you miss a hook, people immediately call you a "долбаеб" (or worse). Even if that hits you emotionally, is it really so hard to press tab and mute that person for yourself? Yes, they might be toxic. Yes, they might be rude. But they could also be saying useful things that might help you now or later. For example, someone might shout, "Ну ты ебаный долбаеб просто дай ульт на зевсе и я дам купол и мы его ебнем!" This is just a rough translation of how it could sound: "u fucking bastard just press ultimate on Zeus and I give chronosphere and we kill him" Part 4: On the Toxicity of the RU Segment Most of the toxic players on the RU server are either men aged 20–40 or trolls who enjoy provoking others with absurd, often nonsensical phrases like: "What u will saying then i give u my dick under ur mouth" "What will u say after sex with animal say it now in VC or text" In Russian, they throw insults that have no exact equivalent in English. Even if people get offended, what’s the problem with muting them? It’s not hard, right? So why should I be forced to suffer because I can’t get my team to group for a teamfight or push a lane, or even do Roshan? Part 5: On the Reporting System Issues I would be so happy if they removed this system from Dota, at least because it interprets trigger words as insults. In the Russian community, saying things like "нахуя тебе", "Похуй мне", "заебал уже", "Отъебись" are common. It’s not that offensive – it’s just how we communicate. You can hear these words in everyday conversations too. But the thing is, many people don’t care, but there are some who know how to exploit the system. They report you for every little thing, even though they might not fully understand the meaning of the sentence For example, if I say: "А нахуя ты это купил ты че ебнулся?" It’s not an insult – it’s a question with a slight tone of mockery about their purchase. I have to pretend to be some aristocrat who grew up in a monastery and never used a swear word just because someone reported me, either from my team or the enemy team. It’s frustrating, especially when players use reports as a joke, just spamming them on anyone, hoping it will work Part 7: How the System Should Change Please, remove or change this system to something more reasonable. Description Dear Valve Support Team, I am writing to formally raise a serious concern regarding persistent racism within the Dota 2 community and the apparent ineffectiveness of the in-game reporting system to address it. 1. Display of Racist Language Across Platforms It is deeply troubling that openly racist terms, such as “Ching Chong,” are allowed to appear in various parts of the game — including player chat, guild names, guild introductions, and even user IDs. These terms are universally recognized as racial slurs targeting Chinese and East Asian communities, and their continued visibility in Dota 2 is unacceptable. Offensive terms like the F-word are rightly censored or filtered out, so why are racial slurs not held to the same standard? 2. Ineffective Reporting System My friends and I have reported a specific guild multiple times for promoting such racism. Despite repeated reports, the guild remains active and the offensive content has not been removed. This leads us to question whether these reports are being reviewed at all, and if so, why no action has been taken. The lack of consequences emboldens such behavior and discourages players from trusting or using the report system. 3. Impact on the Chinese Community As a Dota 2 community organizer, I represent a Chinese Dota 2 community with over 4,000 active members. We host monthly Dota 2 events, all run by passionate volunteers who receive no compensation — we do this purely out of love for the game and a desire to bring people together. However, incidents like this — where racist slurs remain visible and unaddressed — are deeply damaging. They create a hostile environment that discourages participation, especially among Chinese players who are made to feel unwelcome or disrespected. It’s incredibly disheartening for both players and organizers to see our efforts undermined by a lack of moderation and action. Call to Action This issue requires immediate attention. We urge Valve to: • Improve chat and guild content moderation to automatically flag or block known racial slurs. • Enforce stronger review and action on reported offensive content, including timely removal and penalties. • Communicate with the community about steps being taken to combat racism and maintain a respectful gaming environment. Dota 2 is a global game with a diverse player base. There should be no tolerance for racism of any kind. We sincerely hope Valve will take this matter seriously and implement tangible actions to ensure a safe and inclusive environment for all players. Sincerely, Pie ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots Description In September 2023, my behavior score in Dota 2 suddenly dropped from 8580 to 1. It happened literally overnight, and ever since then, I haven’t been able to recover — it’s been almost two years now, and I’m still stuck with the minimum score. During all this time, my behavior score has never gone above 1000, even though I try to play calmly, don’t insult others, don’t use cheats, don’t grief, and generally behave respectfully in every match I honestly have no idea why I received such a harsh penalty, or why it has lasted so long. It feels like either the system glitched, or I got mass-reported — maybe even targeted deliberately. From my experience, once the score drops to 1, the system just doesn’t allow you to climb back up, no matter how clean your behavior is Playing in this state is nearly impossible: matchmaking takes 10 - 15 minutes, and teammates are either leavers, bots, or people who actively ruin the game. Even when I win games and behave perfectly, the system doesn’t seem to increase my score. Description To put it briefly, the issue is, overall, in the politeness system itself. Dota will never have a fully polite player base - it’s become completely normal to hear insults directed at you in video games, especially in Dota. Well, fine. But after the politeness system was introduced in Dota, people didn’t stop insulting, belittling, or humiliating each other. It’s just incredibly naive to add something like this to a game that was practically built around vulgar communication. Personally, I’ve been getting muted for no reason in my last two games, and I honestly don’t like it. I sit there like a caveman, able to ping only once every 30 seconds. I see an enemy hero - “You can use signals again in 30 seconds.” I don’t understand: am I playing a team game, or a whining simulator for kids under 14? In reality, I can’t even ask someone to press Arcane Boots - because apparently, I don’t have enough politeness points. Do Dota players now need to act like tolerant aristocrats? The game is played by people aged 14 to 40 - most have heard insults before, and the mature ones don’t take them personally. I don’t think I should worry about hurting someone’s feelings by pointing out that their clumsy hands and nasally voice in voice chat won’t get them anywhere in life - that their maximum achievement will be working at McDonald’s, asking for orders through tears. Why should others - and I myself - suffer, just because I pointed out one player’s mistakes and got muted for it? I’ve been playing Dota for a long time, and for the past 2 years, I haven’t been able to communicate with teammates properly - because I get muted for asking in chat, “Why the hell are you buying Battle Fury on Sven?” I don’t know - maybe it’s time to just remove the system, or at least redesign it to be stable and sane. In a team game, I can’t talk to my team, point out mistakes, or ask for a teleport via voice - because I lack “politeness”. If I type “TP MID” in all caps - I get muted. If I don’t type it and die - I get reported, and then muted. Pick Techies or Zeus as a position 5? - Report and mute. Don’t give last pick to mid or carry? - Report and mute. Point out someone’s mistake, even calmly? — Report and mute. Respond to provocation? - The instigator stays unmuted, you get muted. Stay silent to avoid mute? - You still get reported, muted, and insulted anyway. Refuse to help a carry because it’ll get you both killed? - Report and mute. Ask a drunk to shut up? - Report and mute. AFK for more than 3 seconds? - Report and mute. Trying to win by playing Broodmother, Lone Druid, Beastmaster, or Brewmaster? - Report from every enemy player, and a mute too. Ask someone “Are you okay?” - Aggression in response, report and mute. Just delete this system. If people can't handle hearing the truth, let them mute others individually like it was before and play in peace. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 8346471869 - 31:00 ### Screenshots Description Hello Valve team, I’m writing as a long-time Dota 2 player who cares deeply about the game and its community. I’d like to offer a suggestion regarding the report and behavior score system. Currently, players can be punished through reports and receive low behavior scores without any possibility to appeal or explain their side. While I understand that the system is designed to be automated to reduce moderation overhead, I believe this approach can sometimes be unfair, especially in nuanced or comeback games. For example, in one of my recent matches, I had a rough early game (0/13/2), but I stayed in the match, farmed, came back strong (11+ kills), and nearly helped my team win. Despite my efforts and good intentions, I was reported—most likely because of my early deaths—and punished, even though I contributed to the game’s comeback. Situations like this are not rare. Without a way to explain context or contest a report, players can feel demoralized or wrongly punished for simply having a bad start or playing in an unconventional but effective way. **Suggestion:** Please consider implementing an optional system that allows players to appeal specific reports or penalties—perhaps with a cooldown or review threshold to avoid abuse. Even just a feedback log showing which reports were most influential and what behavior triggered them would improve transparency. This change could make the system feel more fair, reduce frustration, and encourage players to stay engaged even during hard games—knowing they won’t be automatically punished just for struggling. Thanks for your time and all the work you do to keep Dota 2 going strong.
